name: Nai
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Honsberger, Murray, Carol Honsberger & Ian Tupper (eds.). 2008. Kwomtari Phonology and Grammar Essentials. Data Papers on Papua New Guinea Languages 55. Ukarumpa: SIL-PNG.
sources.note: Describes the SISTER language Kwomtari [kwo], not Nai: stress non-contrastive and hard to hear, first syllable of a bisyllabic word 'often sounds stronger' with rising pitch on the second, schwa syllables unstressed. Mentions Nai only in the classification discussion (pp. 3-4, dialect/lexicostatistics), never its stress.
sources.venue: Data Papers on Papua New Guinea Languages

sources.citation: Honeyman, Thomas. 2017. A grammar of Momu, a language of Papua New Guinea. PhD thesis, ANU.
sources.note: Nothing about Nai/Biaka stress; mentions Biaka only for its nine vowels (citing Hamlin 1998), dual pronouns, body-part counting (Hamlin & Hamlin 2011) and serial verbs.

sources.citation: Hamlin, Newton & Susan Hamlin. 2011. Nai (Biaka) numerals, data supplied to Eugene S. L. Chan, Numeral Systems of the World's Languages (MPI-EVA).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; only the 1-23 body-part counting list with two vowel-quality remarks ('the u being a lax high back vowel'; 'first o is a lax mid front..').

sources.citation: Baron, Wietze. 2007-2023. The Kwomtari Phylum (website, kwomtari.net); Wikipedia 'Nai language'.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; classification, village census and links to Fas materials only.

sources.citation: Baron, Wietze. 1983. Kwomtari Survey. Unpublished manuscript, SIL Survey office, Ukarumpa, 42 pp. (posted at kwomtari.net; Glottolog ref 107948).
sources.note: Nothing for Biaka/Nai: the 100-item wordlists for Fas, Baibai, Kwomtari, Biaka and Guriaso carry no stress marks and the text has no phonology section; the single note 'underscore marks stress!' (p. 38) heads the Pyu list copied from Laycock 1972, not the Biaka data.

sources.citation: Hamlin, Newton B. 1998. Nai verb morphology. MA thesis, University of South Carolina, Columbia. ix+139 pp. (OCLC 39716111). Reissued/revised as Hamlin 2002, unpublished ms., 131 pp. (SIL-PNG).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only grammar sketch of Nai; Honeyman 2017 cites it for the nine-vowel phoneme inventory, so it contains a phonology chapter that is the one place a first-hand stress statement for Nai could exist. Hammarström holds a scan (hh.bib fn papua/).

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.note: Survey chapter with a Kwomtari-family section; would at most repeat Honsberger et al. 2008 on Kwomtari, but is the standard secondary reference to check before declaring the family undescribed for stress.

sources.note: Not seen (both download attempts of the sil.org PDF returned an automated-access block page). SIL-PNG Organised Phonology Data sheets follow a fixed template (phoneme chart, wordlist by phoneme, syllable patterns, phonological and orthographic conventions) in which suprasegmentals (contrastive stress or tone, if any) are normally stated; this 4-page sheet, based on 6 years of SIL work and checked by Hamlin in October 1992 per the search snippet, is the only first-hand phonology statement for Nai located and is the place a tone/no-tone statement would be. Content regarding tone unverified.
